episode.title: Preserve dangerous-command detection across embedded newlines
episode.before: At parent commit 7b23dbfe6841002328f96e8d97980e1d11410db5, dangerous-command patterns were evaluated with re.IGNORECASE only. Patterns using `.*` therefore could not span newline characters, allowing multiline forms of remote-content piping, disk-copy, and recursive-permission commands to avoid detection and proceed without the intended approval boundary.
episode.after: At commit 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625, the detector evaluates every dangerous-command pattern with re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL, so `.` also matches newlines. Four regression cases require multiline curl-to-shell, wget-to-shell, dd, and recursive chmod commands to be classified as dangerous.
episode.diff: The implementation changes the shared regular-expression search flags in tools/approval.py from re.IGNORECASE to re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL without changing the pattern catalog or approval policy. The test suite adds a TestMultilineBypass group with four adversarial commands containing line continuations/newlines. The shared detector remains upstream of terminal execution: terminal_tool delegates to check_dangerous_command before executing non-forced commands, and that orchestration invokes detect_dangerous_command before approval-state handling.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625 is the single-parent implementation commit for issue 232/PR 233; its parent is 7b23dbfe6841002328f96e8d97980e1d11410db5 and it changes tools/approval.py plus tests/tools/test_approval.py.
In the parent state, detect_dangerous_command lowercased the command and searched each dangerous pattern using re.IGNORECASE alone.
The implementation adds re.DOTALL to the flags passed to re.search, causing dot expressions in the existing pattern catalog to span newline characters.

The dangerous-pattern catalog includes dot-based expressions for remote-content piping, disk copying, recursive chmod, recursive chown, SQL DELETE qualification, xargs, and find operations, so the shared flag controls whether these expressions can match across lines.
check_dangerous_command invokes detect_dangerous_command before consulting approval state or prompting; commands classified as non-dangerous are immediately approved by this orchestration path.
The terminal execution path delegates to the consolidated approval module and checks a command before execution when force is false; an unapproved result returns without executing the command.
evidence_units.source: git show 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625:tools/terminal_tool.py, approval imports and wrapper lines 128-140; execution guard lines 885-896

evidence_units.claim: Four regression tests exercise newline-separated curl-to-sh, wget-to-bash, dd with if=, and recursive chmod with 777, and each asserts that detect_dangerous_command returns is_dangerous=True.

The existing approval tests already cover corresponding single-line dangerous forms and benign commands, preserving the detector's broader classification contract while the new cases extend it to multiline input.
evidence_units.source: git show 7166647ca132d54149af35dfd21312a1e3c19625:tests/tools/test_approval.py, existing detector tests lines 1-158

candidate_atomics.name: enable-multiline-policy-matching
candidate_atomics.title: Make policy patterns span embedded newlines
candidate_atomics.description: Adjust the shared pattern-matching semantics so dangerous constructs remain recognizable when their relevant tokens are separated by newline characters.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent newline insertion from bypassing the command classification that gates potentially dangerous effects.
semantic_action.pre_state: The classifier applies dot-based dangerous-command patterns with case-insensitive matching, but dot expressions stop at newlines and may return a non-dangerous classification for split commands.
semantic_action.post_state: The same pattern catalog is evaluated with dot matching extended across newlines, so covered dangerous constructs retain their classification when split across lines.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise representative dot-based patterns with relevant tokens separated by newlines and require a dangerous result while retaining the existing single-line and benign-command test contract.

candidate_atomics.name: lock-multiline-bypass-regressions
candidate_atomics.title: Add adversarial multiline classification cases
candidate_atomics.description: Encode representative newline-based bypasses as regression tests for the shared classifier.

semantic_action.intent: Make future changes detect regressions that reopen newline-based bypasses of the approval boundary.
semantic_action.pre_state: The test suite covers dangerous command detection but has no explicit oracle for tokens separated by embedded newlines.
semantic_action.post_state: The regression suite explicitly requires remote-content piping, disk-copy, and recursive-permission examples containing newlines to be classified as dangerous.
semantic_action.validation: Run the detector test module and require all four multiline cases, together with the pre-existing classification tests, to pass.

candidate_workflows.name: close-multiline-policy-bypass
candidate_workflows.title: Close newline-based bypasses in a pre-execution command policy
candidate_workflows.description: A bounded workflow for repairing a regex-driven effect gate when dangerous constructs are recognized on one line but evade classification after newline insertion.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure commands covered by an existing dangerous-pattern policy cannot bypass its pre-execution approval path merely by inserting newlines.
when_to_use: A pre-execution policy classifier uses regular expressions containing dot expressions over complete command text.
A known dangerous construct is detected in single-line form but is not detected when semantically connected tokens are separated by a newline.
anti_goals: Do not broaden or replace the dangerous-command pattern catalog when changing match traversal alone is sufficient.
Do not alter approval scopes, prompting behavior, environment exemptions, force semantics, or command execution behavior.
Do not normalize away arbitrary whitespace or rewrite the command that will actually be executed.
not_applicable_when: The policy intentionally evaluates each line as an independent command with no cross-line constructs.
The bypass is caused by missing dangerous-operation coverage rather than newline-sensitive matching.
The matcher already spans newlines and the failure originates in parsing, canonicalization, shell semantics, or a downstream approval-state defect.
inputs: The exact command text reaching the classifier
The existing dangerous-pattern catalog and matching flags
The pre-execution call path that consumes the classifier result
Representative single-line and newline-separated dangerous commands
Existing benign-command and classification regression cases
workflow_graph.entry_state: A dangerous effect is gated by a shared classifier, but at least one covered construct can receive a non-dangerous result after newline insertion and consequently avoid the intended approval decision.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Existing policy patterns retain their intended single-line behavior and representative covered constructs split across newlines are classified as dangerous before terminal execution.

steps.condition: Use when inspection confirms the affected patterns rely on dot expressions over whole-command input and the current flags do not allow dot to cross newlines.
steps.validation: Confirm the shared search operation enables newline-spanning dot semantics without modifying the pattern catalog or approval orchestration.

steps.condition: Add cases for each evidenced bypass family fixed by the matching change.
steps.validation: Require newline-separated remote-content pipelines, disk-copy syntax, and recursive-permission syntax to return a dangerous classification; also run the existing detector cases.

validation_ladder: Inspect the classifier and prove that the failing patterns contain dot expressions whose behavior differs at newline boundaries.
Confirm the production call path passes the complete command to the shared classifier before execution and consumes a dangerous result through the approval boundary.
Run focused multiline regression cases for multiple pattern families.
Run the complete command-approval test module to check existing dangerous and benign classifications.
If dependencies permit, run the broader terminal-tool test suite to detect integration regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop if the reported command cannot be reproduced as a newline-sensitive mismatch in the shared classifier.
Stop and select a parsing or pattern-coverage repair if the failure persists when dot already spans newlines.
Do not complete the workflow if multiline dangerous cases pass but established benign or single-line classification tests regress.
Defer execution-based validation when the repository's test runner or dependencies are unavailable, and report that limitation explicitly.
